summary: Four implementable S&R subagent specs for Indian NSE monthly stock options on Shoonya data: (1) oi_walls — put/call OI walls with ATR-normalized headroom scoring and a strict per-strike liquidity guard; (2) gamma_levels — full retail-data GEX pipeline: Black-Scholes IV inversion by bisection (r=7%, q=0) from bid/ask mids, gamma per strike, naive-convention GEX = Γ·OI·S²·0.01 (calls +, puts −), gamma flip via re-evaluation of the GEX profile at each strike level with linear interpolation, scored on regime + room-to-gamma-wall; (3) max_pain — argmin of aggregate option writer pain, small weight, scored by pull direction scaled by days-to-expiry relevance; (4) pivot_levels — floor-trader pivots + prior-day H/L from daily candles as the options-free fallback, scored by ATR-normalized headroom to the next level. All scores are 0-100 per direction, computable in well under 1s from a cached chain snapshot, with explicit neutral-50 fallbacks when the monthly chain is illiquid.

algorithms.name: OI Walls (Put/Call OI Support & Resistance)
algorithms.inputs: spot = cash lp from touchline; chain snapshot for the current monthly expiry: dict {strike: {ce:{oi,v,lp,bp1,sp1}, pe:{oi,v,lp,bp1,sp1}}} covering >=10 strikes each side of ATM (GetOptionChain cnt=10 + cached GetQuotes per strike, refreshed every 5 min); lot_size and expiry date from Shoonya scrip master; ATR_ref (see notes); signal direction.
algorithms.steps: 1. Compute ATR_ref = ATR(14) on daily candles; if daily series unavailable, ATR_ref = ATR(14, 5m) * 8.66 (sqrt of 75 five-min bars/session). 2. Infer strike_step = median of diffs of sorted strikes. 3. Per-strike-side liquidity guard: CE at strike K is VALID iff oi_ce(K) >= min_oi_lots*lot_size AND (v_ce(K) >= 1*lot_size OR (bp1>0 and sp1>0 and (sp1-bp1)/((sp1+bp1)/2) <= max_rel_spread)). Same rule for PE. 4. Chain liquidity check: require >= 3 VALID CE strikes and >= 3 VALID PE strikes, with at least 1 VALID CE at K >= spot and 1 VALID PE at K <= spot. If it fails, return buy=50, sell=50, flag='illiquid_chain' (orchestrator shifts this agent's weight to pivot_levels). 5. call_wall = argmax over VALID CE strikes with K >= spot of oi_ce(K); None if no such strike (upside breakout state). put_wall = argmax over VALID PE strikes with K <= spot of oi_pe(K); None likewise. 6. Wall strength: str_c = oi_ce(call_wall)/median(oi_ce over all VALID CE strikes); str_p analogous. Wall is WEAK if strength < strength_min. 7. Normalized distances: d_res = (call_wall - spot)/ATR_ref; d_sup = (spot - put_wall)/ATR_ref. 8. Score per formulas below; round to int, clip 0-100. Ties in argmax: pick strike closest to spot (nearer wall is the binding one).
algorithms.buy_score_logic: room = 0.75 if call_wall is None else clip(d_res / room_full, 0, 1); if call wall WEAK: room = max(room, 0.6). support = 0.40 if put_wall is None else clip(1 - d_sup / sup_full, 0, 1); if put wall WEAK: support *= 0.6. BUY = round(65*room + 35*support). Interpretation: full 65 room points only when the nearest significant call wall is >= 1.5 daily-ATR above spot; a call wall right on top of spot zeroes the room and blocks the BUY.
algorithms.sell_score_logic: Exact mirror: room = 0.75 if put_wall is None else clip(d_sup / room_full, 0, 1); if put wall WEAK: room = max(room, 0.6). resistance_backstop = 0.40 if call_wall is None else clip(1 - d_res / sup_full, 0, 1); if call wall WEAK: resistance_backstop *= 0.6. SELL = round(65*room + 35*resistance_backstop). A put wall just under spot blocks the SELL; a call wall just overhead supports it.
algorithms.default_weight: 0.35 buy / 0.35 sell within the S&R family — OI walls are the most robust option-derived level on illiquid monthly stock chains because they need only OI, not clean premiums.
algorithms.data_requirements: GetOptionChain (NFO, monthly expiry, cnt=10) then GetQuotes per strike for oi/v/bp1/sp1 — fetch once per signal and cache 5 min; oi and lp also stream on the touchline websocket if strikes are pre-subscribed. UNIT CHECK (do once per deployment): Shoonya oi for NFO is in units (shares); if it matches NSE-website contract counts instead, multiply all OI thresholds and comparisons by lot_size. If GetOptionChain errors or returns < 4 strikes, return neutral 50 with flag 'no_chain'.
algorithms.params: min_oi_lots=3; max_rel_spread=0.25; room_full=1.5 (daily ATRs for full headroom); sup_full=1.5; strength_min=1.5; chain window=+/-10 strikes; refresh=300s.

algorithms.name: Gamma Exposure Levels (GEX walls + gamma flip)
algorithms.inputs: spot (cash lp); chain snapshot as in oi_walls but only +/-6 strikes around ATM (13 strikes, 26 options): per option oi, lp, bp1, sp1, v; lot_size; expiry datetime (from scrip master 'exd' field — do NOT hardcode the weekday, NSE has changed expiry days); r=0.07, q=0.0; ATR_ref; current IST timestamp.
algorithms.steps: 1. ATM strike = argmin |K - spot|; window = 13 strikes centered there (fewer if chain smaller). 2. Option price selection: mid = (bp1+sp1)/2 if bp1>0 and sp1>0 and (sp1-bp1)/mid <= 0.25, else lp if v>0 (traded today), else SKIP the option. Also SKIP if price <= intrinsic + 0.05 (IV undefined/garbage). 3. T = max((expiry@15:30 IST - now).total_seconds() / (365*86400), 0.5/365). 4. Black-Scholes (q=0): d1 = (ln(S/K) + (r + 0.5*sigma^2)*T) / (sigma*sqrt(T)); d2 = d1 - sigma*sqrt(T); Call = S*N(d1) - K*exp(-r*T)*N(d2); Put = K*exp(-r*T)*N(-d2) - S*N(-d1). Use S = cash spot (r=7% doubles as carry proxy; using the futures price with r=0 is an acceptable variant). 5. IV inversion per option by BISECTION (monotone in sigma, no vega blowups): lo=0.03, hi=4.0; iterate <=60 times; stop when |model - market| < 0.05 or hi-lo < 1e-4; if f(lo) and f(hi) same sign, SKIP option. 6. If total options with valid IV < min_iv_strikes: fallback FLAT VOL — sigma_flat = (C_atm + P_atm) / (0.8 * S * sqrt(T)) (Brenner-Subrahmanyam straddle approximation) using ATM prices from step 2; if even those are unusable, return buy=50, sell=50, flag='no_iv'. Apply sigma_flat to all strikes. 7. Gamma (identical for call and put, q=0): Gamma(S,K,sigma,T) = phi(d1) / (S * sigma * sqrt(T)), phi = standard normal pdf. Use CE-implied sigma for the call leg and PE-implied sigma for the put leg; if one side lacks IV, reuse the other side's sigma at that strike (same-strike IVs must match by parity). 8. Per-strike GEX (naive dealer convention, rupees of dealer-hedge delta-notional per 1% spot move): GEX_K = (Gamma_c(K)*OI_c(K) - Gamma_p(K)*OI_p(K)) * S^2 * 0.01, with OI in units/shares (see unit check in oi_walls). SIGN ASSUMPTION: dealers are net LONG calls (customers write covered calls) and net SHORT puts (customers buy protective puts) — the SqueezeMetrics naive convention. Documented caveats to put in the code comment: (a) OI carries no long/short side information; (b) on single stocks, retail speculative call BUYING inverts the call sign, so treat GEX as a heuristic, not ground truth — this is why the weight is modest; (c) monthly stock-option IVs are noisy, so per-strike GEX magnitude matters less than the sign pattern and strike locations. 9. Gamma walls: K_pos = strike with max positive GEX_K (the pinning/wall strike); split views: K_res = strike with max positive GEX among K >= spot, K_sup = max positive GEX among K <= spot (None if absent). 10. Gamma flip: define g(x) = sum over window strikes K of (Gamma(x,K,sigma_cK,T)*OI_c - Gamma(x,K,sigma_pK,T)*OI_p) * x^2 * 0.01, holding per-strike sigmas FIXED; evaluate g at each strike level x in the window (13 evaluations x 26 gammas — trivial, well under 50 ms). Find the sign change of g between adjacent strikes CLOSEST to spot and linearly interpolate: flip = x_i + (0 - g_i)*(x_{i+1} - x_i)/(g_{i+1} - g_i). If g is positive everywhere: flip = lowest strike - strike_step (firmly positive-gamma regime); negative everywhere: flip = highest strike + strike_step. 11. Expiry damping: if T <= 2/365, gamma is explosive and pin risk dominates — after computing the score, shrink toward neutral: score = 50 + (score-50)*0.7. 12. Cache all IVs/gammas for 5 minutes; only step 10 onward needs re-running when spot moves within the cache window.
algorithms.buy_score_logic: regime = clip(0.5 + (spot - flip)/(2*ATR_ref), 0, 1) — above the flip dealers are long gamma and buy dips, which directly supports a mean-reversion BUY; room = 0.75 if K_res is None else clip((K_res - spot)/ATR_ref, 0, 1) — a large positive-GEX strike just overhead acts as a pin/lid; sup = 0.40 if K_sup is None else clip(1 - (spot - K_sup)/ATR_ref, 0, 1) — a positive-GEX strike just below is a dealer-defended floor. BUY = round(40*regime + 35*room + 25*sup), then apply step-11 expiry damping.
algorithms.sell_score_logic: regime_sell = 1 - regime (below the flip dealers amplify downside moves, supporting the short); room_sell = 0.75 if K_sup is None else clip((spot - K_sup)/ATR_ref, 0, 1) — the positive-GEX floor below is the obstacle for a SELL; shield = 0.40 if K_res is None else clip(1 - (K_res - spot)/ATR_ref, 0, 1) — a gamma lid just overhead caps rallies and protects the short. SELL = round(40*regime_sell + 35*room_sell + 25*shield), then expiry damping.
algorithms.default_weight: 0.25 buy / 0.25 sell — informative regime/level signal but the dealer-sign assumption is least reliable on single stocks, so it stays below oi_walls.
algorithms.data_requirements: Same chain snapshot as oi_walls but requires usable premiums (bp1/sp1 or traded lp), not just OI — hence the stricter per-option skip rules. Needs expiry date from the NFO scrip master and a synchronized IST clock for T. No greeks/IV from Shoonya, everything is computed. If fewer than min_iv_strikes options yield IV and the flat-vol fallback also fails, return 50/50 with flag 'no_iv' so the orchestrator reweights to oi_walls + pivot_levels.
algorithms.params: window=6 strikes each side; r=0.07; q=0.0; bisection lo=0.03, hi=4.0, max_iter=60, price_tol=0.05, sigma_tol=1e-4; max_rel_spread=0.25; intrinsic_pad=0.05; min_iv_strikes=4; T_floor=0.5/365; dte_damp_threshold=2 days, damp_factor=0.7; regime_scale=2*ATR_ref; room_scale=1*ATR_ref; cache_ttl=300s.

algorithms.name: Max Pain Pull
algorithms.inputs: Full chain snapshot (+/-10 strikes, same object as oi_walls): oi_ce and oi_pe per strike; spot; expiry date; ATR_ref; direction.
algorithms.steps: 1. Candidate strikes = all strikes in the snapshot with oi_ce(K) + oi_pe(K) > 0. Guard: require >= 5 candidate strikes AND sum of all OI >= 20*lot_size; else return buy=50, sell=50, flag='illiquid_chain'. 2. For each candidate settlement level Ks in the strike list compute writer pain: pain(Ks) = sum over all strikes K of [oi_ce(K)*max(0, Ks - K) + oi_pe(K)*max(0, K - Ks)] (lot size and rupee scaling cancel in the argmin — omit them). 3. MP = argmin pain(Ks); on ties pick the Ks closest to spot. 4. DTE = calendar days from today to expiry date. 5. relevance = clip(1 - DTE/15, 0.2, 1.0) — the pin-to-max-pain effect is an expiry-week phenomenon; far from expiry the agent deliberately hugs neutral. 6. pull_norm = clip((MP - spot) / (1.5*ATR_ref), -1, 1) — positive means the chain 'pulls' price upward toward MP. 7. Score per formulas below. Cost: <=21 strikes x 21 candidates = 441 multiply-adds, microseconds.
algorithms.buy_score_logic: BUY = round(50 + 50 * pull_norm * relevance). MP one and a half daily ATRs above spot in expiry week scores 100; MP far below spot in expiry week scores near 0; any configuration more than ~3 weeks from expiry stays within 50 +/- 10.
algorithms.sell_score_logic: SELL = round(50 - 50 * pull_norm * relevance). Exact mirror: MP below spot supports the short.
algorithms.default_weight: 0.10 buy / 0.10 sell — max pain is a weak, slow magnet with mixed empirical support; it should nudge, never veto.
algorithms.data_requirements: Only per-strike OI from the cached GetOptionChain/GetQuotes snapshot — the most illiquidity-tolerant options agent since it never touches premiums. Recompute at most every 5 minutes (OI updates are slow intraday). On missing chain, return neutral 50 with flag.
algorithms.params: pull_scale=1.5 (ATR_ref multiples for full pull); dte_full=15 days; relevance_floor=0.2; min_candidate_strikes=5; min_total_oi_lots=20.

algorithms.name: Floor-Trader Pivot Levels (options-free fallback S&R)
algorithms.inputs: Prior trading day's H, L, C; spot; ATR_ref; direction. No options data.
algorithms.steps: 1. Get prior-day OHLC: primary — Shoonya daily series (get_daily_price_series / TPSeries daily), take the last completed session; fallback — aggregate the cached 5m history: group bars by IST session date (09:15-15:30), take max(inth)/min(intl)/last(intc) of the most recent date strictly before today. This agent must NEVER return 'no data' if 5m history exists. 2. Pivots: P=(H+L+C)/3; R1=2P-L; S1=2P-H; R2=P+(H-L); S2=P-(H-L); R3=H+2(P-L); S3=L-2(H-P). Level set = {P,R1,R2,R3,S1,S2,S3, PDH=H, PDL=L} (9 levels). 3. Cluster: sort ascending; merge any run of levels whose successive gaps are < cluster_tol*ATR_ref into one level at their mean, recording count n (n>=2 = strong cluster). 4. R_star = smallest merged level > spot (None if spot above all); S_star = largest merged level < spot (None if below all). 5. head_up = (R_star - spot)/ATR_ref; dist_dn = (spot - S_star)/ATR_ref. 6. Score per formulas; round and clip 0-100. Runs in microseconds; recompute pivots once per day at session start, only steps 4-6 per signal.
algorithms.buy_score_logic: room = 1.0 if R_star is None (blue-sky above R3/PDH) else clip(head_up / room_full, 0, 1); if R_star is a cluster (n>=2): room *= 0.85 (merged pivot+PDH barriers are stronger). support = 0.30 if S_star is None else clip(1 - dist_dn / sup_full, 0, 1); if S_star is a cluster: support = min(1, support*1.15). BUY = round(65*room + 35*support).
algorithms.sell_score_logic: Mirror: room = 1.0 if S_star is None else clip(dist_dn / room_full, 0, 1); cluster S_star: room *= 0.85. resistance_backstop = 0.30 if R_star is None else clip(1 - head_up / sup_full, 0, 1); cluster R_star: *1.15 capped at 1. SELL = round(65*room + 35*resistance_backstop).
algorithms.default_weight: 0.30 buy / 0.30 sell — always computable and unaffected by option illiquidity; becomes weight 1.0 within the family whenever the chain-based agents flag 'illiquid_chain'/'no_chain'/'no_iv'.
algorithms.data_requirements: Daily candles via Shoonya get_daily_price_series (fetch once at 09:15 IST, cache all day); guaranteed fallback from the 5m TPSeries history that arrives with every signal. No websocket or REST call needed at signal time.
algorithms.params: room_full=1.0 (daily ATRs to nearest opposing level for full room); sup_full=0.75; cluster_tol=0.15; cluster_room_penalty=0.85; cluster_support_bonus=1.15; blue_sky_room=1.0; missing_support_component=0.30.

notes: SHARED CONVENTIONS (implement once in a util module): (1) ATR_ref = ATR(14) on daily candles (Wilder smoothing); fallback ATR(14) on 5m bars * 8.66 (= sqrt(75) five-min bars per NSE session) when dailies are missing — this is the single normalizer used by all four agents so scores are comparable across stocks of any price. (2) clip(x,lo,hi) = min(max(x,lo),hi); all final scores rounded ints in [0,100]; 50 = neutral/no-information. (3) Chain snapshot schema handed to agents: {strike: {'ce': {'oi','v','lp','bp1','sp1'}, 'pe': {...}}} plus lot_size, expiry_datetime (from scrip-master exd — never hardcode the expiry weekday), fetched via GetOptionChain(cnt=10) + GetQuotes per strike and cached 300s; the 26 GetQuotes calls are the latency bottleneck, so fetch them when the RSI/W%R setup starts forming, not at trigger time. (4) OI unit check (one-time, per deployment): NSE websites quote OI in contracts, broker feeds usually in units/shares — compare one strike; if Shoonya returns contracts, multiply by lot_size everywhere OI is compared to lot-based thresholds and in GEX. (5) Fallback protocol: any options agent returning flag in {'illiquid_chain','no_chain','no_iv'} must still return buy=50/sell=50; the orchestrator renormalizes the S&R family weights onto the agents that did produce information (worst case pivot_levels alone at 1.0). (6) All timestamps IST; T uses ACT/365 with expiry at 15:30 IST. GEX methodology sources: Perfiliev 'How to Calculate Gamma Exposure and Zero Gamma Level' (https://perfiliev.com/blog/how-to-calculate-gamma-exposure-and-zero-gamma-level/), SqueezeMetrics GEX white paper (https://squeezemetrics.com/monitor/download/pdf/white_paper.pdf), SpotGamma GEX overview (https://spotgamma.com/gamma-exposure-gex/), GEXBoard zero-gamma/flip explainer (https://gexboard.com/learn/zero-gamma-gamma-flip). Known limitation to record in docs: the GEX dealer-sign convention is a market-wide heuristic calibrated on index options; on single NSE stocks with heavy speculative call buying the call-side sign can invert, which is why gamma_levels carries less weight than oi_walls despite being more sophisticated.
